name: Can pool fill-in be done in winter or during rainy season?

mainEntity.name: Is it okay to do a pool fill-in during the rainy season in Southern California?
mainEntity.text: Is it okay to do a pool fill-in during the rainy season in Southern California?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pool fill-in can be performed during cooler or wetter months, but weather matters a lot. Rain can turn access paths into mud, make excavation more difficult, and interfere with proper compaction. Wet fill material is harder to compact consistently, and runoff can carry silt or debris into adjacent areas. In Southern California, the rainy season can also slow inspections and grading work. Contractors often prefer dry conditions because the equipment performs better and the finished grade is easier to shape. If the project must happen in winter, the contractor should explain how mud, runoff, and erosion will be managed. Homeowners should ask whether the schedule includes weather contingency time and whether any temporary ground protection will be used. A wet-season job is possible, but it needs tighter site control.
acceptedAnswer.description: It can be done, but wet weather can make pool fill-in harder because muddy access, poor compaction, and runoff control become bigger issues. Rain can delay hauling, grading, and inspections. Many contractors prefer drier conditions for better equipment access and more reliable compaction.
